topic: Germany is decided in your first IB year
text:
Almost everything on this site is a question a student can still act on. Germany is the exception. Whether a German university will accept an IB Diploma at all turns on the shape of the Diploma — two languages, a natural science, Mathematics, a social science among the six — and that is settled when subjects are chosen, usually at sixteen.

The practical upshot is unusual enough to be worth stating plainly: a student who might want Germany should read the KMK rule before they finalise subjects, and a student in their final year should read it to find out where they stand rather than to change anything. Excellent points do not compensate for the wrong combination, and no supplementary course repairs it afterwards.
attribution: The KMK agreement on recognition of the IB Diploma, in the version of 15 June 2023
whatThisIsNot: Not a reason to avoid Germany, and not a claim that the combination is exotic. Many IB students satisfy it without trying. The point is to check rather than assume.
